title: Committee of Supply − Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: Proactive help for distressed families
sections.summary: Asks what the Ministry does to proactively seek out families showing signs of distress and coordinate assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Proactively seeking them out and offering timely interventions will give such Singaporeans more breathing room to focus on their jobs or studies, both of which are essential in ensuring their families' longer-term independence and success.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, may I know what the Ministry is doing to proactively seek out families showing signs of distress, such as escalating arrears in rent, utilities and service and conservancy charges (S&CC)?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: How is the Ministry coordinating the assistance necessary to help these families stay afloat and progress?

sections.label: KidSTART programme update
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry for an update on KidSTART's implementation and observations so far.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As such, when KidSTART was announced last year, I was very heartened as it supports the provision of a conducive environment for low-income and vulnerable children in their early years so as to give them a good start.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, could the Ministry provide an update on the implementation and observations made so far of the KidSTART programme?

sections.label: Help for unwed parents
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry helps children in such situations, including interim housing for unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As such, how does the Ministry help children in such situations?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For example, will there be interim arrangements to home unwed parents and their children till they are eligible to purchase a flat of their own?

sections.label: Supporting parents and families
sections.summary: Asks what the Ministry does to support parents or, where parents are absent, the families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask what is the Ministry doing to support parents better or, in instances where parents are absent, the families?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We need to continue to minimise the income inequality which risks undermining the precious social cohesion that we enjoy today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We need to help families in or at risk of financial distress to stand tall and strong again.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We need to ensure that all children of Singapore have equal opportunities, good access to resources and have their potential developed to the fullest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We must continue to strengthen our foundations for the future of Singapore and for the betterment of our children and theirs.

sections.label: Congratulatory messages for centenarians
sections.summary: Proposes the President send congratulatory messages to centenarians and couples at diamond jubilees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is in this context that I would like to highlight a suggestion that was made to me on how our community can play a signalling role to reinforce family values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I propose that our President send congratulatory messages to Singaporean centenarians on the occasion of their 100th birthday and every year thereafter, as well as married couples on the occasion of their diamond jubilee and every jubilee thereafter.

sections.label: Manpower for infant care
sections.summary: Asks the Ministry's plans to fill manpower shortages in infant care and explore new job roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To make sure our children receive quality care and education in their foundation years, the Government and, specifically, ECDA, has made substantial investments in the early childhood sector over the past years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given the rapid expansion of childcare facilities in recent years, what are the Ministry's plans to fill shortages in manpower, especially in the area of infant care?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can we explore new job roles, such as that of an allied role, to support and complement the work of the infant and childcare teachers?

sections.label: Registry of allied care-takers
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will explore setting up a registry of allied care-takers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry also explore setting up a registry of allied care-takers?

sections.label: Childcare and infant care centres growth
sections.summary: Childcare centres grew by two-thirds from 2008 to 2015, and infant care centres by 245%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since the number of births began its somewhat tentative recovery from the record lows around a decade ago, we have seen a large increase in childcare centres, with the number growing by two-thirds from 2008 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The number of centres providing infant care services grew by much more during that time, 245%.

sections.label: Excess capacity and demand patterns
sections.summary: Excess capacity has existed since 2008, reached 23% in 2015, while demand patterns add pressure.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This suggests that it is not just the quantity of demand that is increasing, the pattern of demand changes is also adding to the pressure on service providers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These gaps occur against a backdrop in which there is not only no shortage of overall capacity, there has, in fact, been excess capacity of around 15% since 2008.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the latest published figures, and even before taking into account the Finance Minister's recent Budget speech update, the excess capacity has been increasing and reached 23% in 2015.

sections.label: No space in Nee Soon South BTOs
sections.summary: According to Childcare Link, no centres in the Nee Soon South BTOs have space now.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to Childcare Link, none of the centres in the Nee Soon South BTOs have any space right now.

sections.label: Subsidies for second or third child
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will consider additional infant care and childcare subsidies for second or third children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In order to encourage more couples to have children, in view of our low fertility rate, will the Government consider offering additional infant care and childcare subsidies for the second or third child?

sections.label: KidSTART programme components and beneficiaries
sections.summary: Asks what KidSTART's components are and how many children and families have benefited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In this respect, I believe KidSTART is a key initiative that can help in this cause of enhancing social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: What are the components of this programme and what is the number of children and families that have benefited from the programme?

sections.label: Minimum school attendance days
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would raise minimum school attendance from one day a month to at least one week a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Considering that one day a month is generally insufficient for the child to develop well in school, would the Ministry consider increasing the minimum number of days of school attendance to at least one week a month instead?

sections.label: Basis for care subsidies
sections.summary: Proposes that subsidies for full-time or part-time care be based solely on family income or per capita income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The quantum of subsidies for full-time or part-time care should be based solely on family income or per capita income instead.

sections.label: Home-based Care Services pilot update
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for an update on the Home-based Care Services pilot programme under SG Enable.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update of the pilot programme for the Home-based Care Services (HBCS) under SG Enable?

sections.label: Caregiver training and monitoring gadgets
sections.summary: Asks if the Ministry will work with MOH on free basic caregiver training and with healthcare providers on a digital gadget information kit.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry work with MOH to provide the caregivers with free essential basic training?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Also, can the Ministry work with healthcare providers to develop an information kit of proven digital gadgets that can be installed at home to assist the caregiver in monitoring?

sections.label: Trained community volunteers for elderly
sections.summary: Suggests training community groups like SCDF myResponder volunteers who register on a system and respond swiftly to nearby elderly calls for help.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: To cater for the diverse needs in our society, we need to cultivate a culture where everyone plays a part, takes ownership of their lives and pays it forward.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I would suggest we train community groups similar to those like the SCDF myResponder volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The trained individuals can register themselves on a system and, when a known case of an elderly calls for help, volunteers within the nearest location can respond swiftly to them.

sections.label: Falling youth drinking, cannabis, smoking rates
sections.summary: States that in 1988 hard-drinkers were 42%, cannabis users 17% and daily smokers 23%, now 5%, 7% and 3%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 1988, their percentage of 15- to 16-year-old hard-drinkers was 42%, and now it is only 5%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their percentage of young cannabis users was 17%, now it is 7%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their percentage of young daily smokers was 23%, now it is 3%.

sections.label: Project Self-Discovery founding
sections.summary: In 1992, with a US$1.2 million government grant, Milkman formed Project Self-Discovery, offering youths natural-high alternatives to drugs and crime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 1992, with a US$1.2 million government grant, Milkman formed Project Self-Discovery, which offered youths natural-high alternative solutions to drugs and crime.

sections.label: Youth in Iceland funding
sections.summary: Kids from low-income families received help to take part, and in Reykjavik each child receives $430 a year for recreational activities under the Youth in Iceland programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Kids from low-income families received help to take part.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, in Reykjavik, each child receives $430 a year to pay for recreational activities that fall under the Youth in Iceland programme.

sections.label: Safe and Secure Families update
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister for an update on the Safe and Secure Families pilot announced last year, focused on family preservation and reunification services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on the Safe and Secure Families pilot announced last year with its attention on "family preservation" and "family reunification" services?

sections.label: Methodist Welfare Services debt scheme
sections.summary: Methodist Welfare Services, in its Jubilee year, began a scheme to help families clear debts with gifts of up to $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Measures like skills upgrading for better jobs or ensuring their children attend school may end up as low priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is the reason why the Methodist Welfare Services, during its Jubilee year, embarked on a scheme to help families clear their debts with gifts of up to $2,000.

sections.label: Methodist Welfare Services debt matching
sections.summary: Methodist Welfare Services started a scheme matching every dollar of debt paid off by clients, up to $100 a month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One such scheme that Methodist Welfare Services has started was to match every dollar of debt paid off by the clients, up to $100 a month.

sections.label: Temporary Assistance and Silver Support
sections.summary: Some Singaporeans receiving both Silver Support and Temporary ComCare assistance were apparently advised their Temporary ComCare assistance might be reduced due to Silver Support payments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another issue about Temporary Assistance that has recently cropped up is how it interacts with the Silver Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some Singaporeans who receive both Silver Support and Temporary ComCare assistance were apparently advised that their Temporary ComCare assistance might be reduced in view of the Silver Support payments.

sections.label: Ad hoc repair funding claims
sections.summary: Recipients may claim up to 70% funding for ad hoc repair expenses, capped at $300 annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: First, allow recipients to claim up to 70% funding for ad hoc repair expenses, such as broken shoes, spectacles, damaged appliances, replacement of faulty light bulbs, up to a maximum claim of $300 annually.

sections.label: One-off household item funding
sections.summary: Recipients may claim one-off 100% funding for household item purchases such as beds and furniture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Second, allow recipients to claim a one-off 100% funding for household item purchases, such as beds, furniture and so on.

sections.label: SSO officers social work training
sections.summary: The question asks how many SSO officers are social work-trained and what requisite training staff receive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how many of the current SSO officers are social work-trained and also what are some of the requisite training provided to the staff?

sections.label: Maintenance records officer appointment
sections.summary: The Minister said last year a maintenance records officer would be appointed to facilitate Court action against defaulters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, the Minister also said last year that a maintenance records officer would be appointed to facilitate firm Court action against incorrigible defaulters.

sections.label: Unwed mothers excluded from benefits
sections.summary: Unwed mothers are still not given the Baby Bonus cash gift and various tax rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, unwed mothers are still not given the Baby Bonus cash gift and various tax rebates.

sections.label: HDB family nucleus for unwed mothers
sections.summary: The speaker urges allowing unwed mothers and one-foreign-spouse families to form a family nucleus for HDB purchase and rental.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fellow Members have spoken about lowering the income cap for rental housing and I repeat the same call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also urge the Government to allow unwed mothers and families consisting of one foreign spouse to form a family nucleus for the purposes of purchase and rental of HDB units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Numerous policies continue to disadvantage unmarried mothers and their children, who are being classified as "illegitimate".

sections.label: Illegitimacy in inheritance and tax
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the use of "illegitimacy" in inheritance and tax reliefs can be done away with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can we do away with the use of "illegitimacy" in inheritance and tax reliefs?

sections.label: Central agency for such families
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministries could consider setting up a central agency for such families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Ministries consider setting up a central agency for such families?

sections.label: Training framework for professional donees
sections.summary: The passage seeks an update on the development of the training and regulatory framework for professional donees and professional deputies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In light of the matters raised during the debates, I would like to get an update on the development of the training and regulatory framework for these professional donees and professional deputies.

sections.label: Vulnerable adults suffering in pain
sections.summary: The passage states that some vulnerable adults suffer in pain because the state cannot enter their homes to give timely assistance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Today, some vulnerable adults are suffering in pain because the state has been unable to enter their homes to give timely assistance.

sections.label: Financial abuse omitted from Vulnerable Adults Act
sections.summary: The passage states the Vulnerable Adults Act covers physical abuse, psychological abuse and neglect but not financial abuse, citing a 2014 study.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Whilst the Vulnerable Adults Act will cover physical abuse, psychological abuse and neglect, there is no mention of financial abuse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: A 2014 study by Trans Safe Centre, a charity that specialises in tackling elder abuse, showed about one in three involved a senior who had been financially abused.

sections.label: Rise in elderly suicides
sections.summary: The passage states the proportion of seniors among those who take their lives each year has risen, citing a near 60% jump in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The proportion of seniors among those who take their lives each year has risen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It had been reported that there was a near 60% jump in elderly suicides in 2014, compared to 2000, and 126 seniors aged 60 and above killed themselves in 2014.

sections.label: MSF funds for scheme
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MSF will consider providing more funds to ensure the scheme's sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will MSF consider providing more funds to ensure sustainability in this scheme?

sections.label: Caregiver and employment support
sections.summary: The passage asks about plans to support caregivers of persons with disabilities and Government efforts to improve their employability and employment options.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What is the plan on supporting caregivers of persons with disabilities on care-giving issues, such as physical and emotional burnout?

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What is the Government doing to improve the employability and employment options of persons with disabilities?

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan Roll-out Committee
sections.summary: The passage suggests setting up an Enabling Masterplan Roll-out Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Suggestion one − set up an Enabling Masterplan Roll-out Committee.

sections.label: EM3 Roll-out Committee proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes an EM3 Roll-out Committee headed by the Minister to give inputs, track and report progress, and encourages mini Enabling Plans by disability groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: More than many other Ministries, this is a Ministry that needs to rely on the ideas, trust and volunteerism of many stakeholders to create accurate, out-of-the-box and impactful social solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I, therefore, propose that an EM3 Roll-out Committee be set up and headed by the Minister himself or someone appointed by the Minister, no less.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Its mission will be to provide inputs to an Implementation Plan; and to track and report on the progress of the EM3 over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Suggestion two − encourage mini Enabling Plans by disability groups so that there is more ownership by them.

sections.label: Review of school-to-work scheme
sections.summary: The passage suggests conducting a review of the school-to-work scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: Suggestion five − conduct a review of the school-to-work scheme.

sections.label: Adults with moderate to severe needs
sections.summary: The passage states options for adults with moderate to severe needs must be studied in work, care-giving and residential living, and warns against last-century mindsets in the EM3.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: This is the most challenging of the groups that we have to support in the disability sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: It is important that the various options for adults with moderate to severe needs be studied carefully in the areas of work, care-giving and residential living.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: In residential living, for instance, there is sufficient literature to look at a continuum of living models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: We need not only look at institutionalised built-up options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: There are more community-based models of partially supported living elsewhere in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: For a sector with many diverse needs with limited resources, the need to deep-dive, innovate, pioneer, scale and persuade other people to join us in solving the many challenges, is very necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: I recently came across an Australian competition in which start-up digital firms pitched their digital ideas to find innovations that will revolutionalise the lives of people with disabilities − 3-D printed prosthetic limbs; a one-stop-shop that stores all the forms the community will ever need in a smart phone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: We must take heed to not populate the EM3 with last-century mindsets, tools and solutions, otherwise, we will be throwing good money after bad and we will be pouring old wine into new wine skin, causing the wine skin to burst.

sections.label: Assistive Technology Fund lifetime cap
sections.summary: The fund has a fixed lifetime cap of $40,000 per person, and the member asks if needs can be assessed case-by-case with flexibility beyond the cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: The fund has a fixed lifetime cap of $40,000 per person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: While the changes that have been made to the scheme are encouraging, we believe that the Assistive Technology Fund can be enhanced if the financial burden for persons with disabilities and special needs is over their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: If required, is it possible for the Ministry to assess the needs of these individuals on a case-by-case basis and exercise flexibility, even if they have exceeded the cap?

sections.label: SG Enable bulk purchasing savings
sections.summary: The member asks whether SG Enable could consolidate orders to negotiate with vendors and pass cost savings to end-consumers, including those just above the income eligibility cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Will it be more cost effective for SG Enable to consolidate these orders, so that it can negotiate with vendors and pass cost savings to the end-consumers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: The benefits of bulk purchasing of assistive technology devices could be extended to those whose household income puts them just above the income eligibility cap but who will still find it onerous to fork out thousands of dollars for an assistive device.

sections.label: Manpower in childcare and social services
sections.summary: The member asks for an update on attracting, retaining and deepening manpower competencies in childcare and social services, noting mid-career candidates can take 1.5 to two years to qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as Singapore matures and ages as a nation, the demand for quality early childhood and social services increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Can the Ministry update on the progress in attracting, retaining and deepening competencies of manpower in the childcare and social services sector?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Mid-career candidates have shared that they can take 1.5 to two years to be qualified to work in these sectors.

sections.label: Number of social workers doubled
sections.summary: According to MSF figures released last year, the number of social workers doubled from 2012 to reach 1,600 in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to figures released by MSF last year, the number of social workers doubled from 2012 to reach 1,600 in 2016.

sections.label: Social work graduate wages gap
sections.summary: Despite pay increments announced in Budget 2015, wages of fresh social work graduates remain a distance from the overall median wage of fresh graduates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Despite pay increments announced in Budget 2015, the wages of fresh graduates in social work are still a distance from the overall median wage of fresh graduates.

sections.label: Government support for families and disabilities
sections.summary: The member welcomes Government support including the Additional CPF Housing Grant for first-timer resale flat couples and expanded infant care capacity, and notes people with disabilities are included in lower-income initiatives like U-Save rebates.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government's support for families, especially the Additional CPF Housing Grant for first-timer couples buying resale flats and the increase in capacity of centre-based infant care to 8,000 by 2020, is, indeed, welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we move towards a more caring and inclusive society, people with disabilities are also included in the Government's initiatives for lower income families, such as the U-Save rebates, to mitigate the increase in water tax.

sections.label: Wage support for disabled hiring
sections.summary: The speaker urges permanent wage support for hiring people with disabilities and notes up to $100 million over five years for VWO and charity capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With that in mind, I urge the Government to consider providing some wage support for companies hiring people with disabilities as a permanent employee, instead of offering them contract-based employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This will give the individuals and their care-giving families more certainty and assurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am also heartened that, over the next five years, the Ministry will provide additional funding, up to $100 million in total, to further develop the capabilities of our VWOs and charities.

sections.label: Charity funds distribution disparity
sections.summary: A report cited that in 2012 small charities received under 1% of funds while large charities took 85%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The same report cited that in 2012, less than 1% of the total funds raised went to small charities with annual receipts of less than $250,000 while large charities with annual receipts of above $10 million took the lion's share of 85%.

sections.label: Community as volunteer resource pool
sections.summary: Given manpower shortage and increasing needs, the community should be looked to as a new resource pool, perhaps through gig volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: With the manpower shortage and increasing needs, we should look more to the community as a new resource pool − perhaps having "gig volunteers".

sections.label: Rallying community for social needs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry will leverage the community more and how to rally, incentivise and organise it for unfulfilled social needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Does the Ministry intend to leverage on them more?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: How can we rally, incentivise and organise the community better to address unfulfilled social needs?

sections.label: MSF support amid economic uncertainty
sections.summary: MSF stands ready to provide additional support to families and individuals facing hard times amid economic uncertainties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Amidst the economic uncertainties, MSF stands ready to provide the necessary additional support to the families and individuals who have fallen on hard times and are trying to bounce back.

sections.label: Extending social and employment pilot
sections.summary: After experimenting at two SSOs last year, the pilot combining social and employment assistance by one SSO officer extends to three more SSOs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Last year, we experimented with bringing together social assistance and employment services under one roof at two SSOs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: This year, we will extend the pilot delivery of both social and employment assistance by the same SSO officer to three more SSOs.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan committee recommendations
sections.summary: The 22-member committee submitted the third Enabling Masterplan to the Ministry in December last year with several recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The third Enabling Masterplan submitted by the 22-member committee to my Ministry in December last year put forth a number of recommendations.

sections.label: KidSTART pilot for vulnerable children
sections.summary: KidSTART was piloted since last July for low-income and vulnerable children who may need additional support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We, too, want every child to have a good start in life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: This is why we piloted KidSTART for low-income and vulnerable children who may need additional support since last July.

sections.label: Children supported at pilot sites
sections.summary: More than 300 children have been supported in three pilot sites.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Today, we have supported more than 300 children in three pilot sites.

sections.label: Support for young couples, future challenges
sections.summary: Young couples now have better support, but ageing, shrinking families and overseas work mean fewer caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We now have better support for young couples as they plan to start families and raise their children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Now, looking ahead, we face different challenges: ageing population, shrinking family sizes and more people working abroad have resulted in fewer members within the family to share the care-giving load.

sections.label: Earlier autism diagnoses in children
sections.summary: More children are being diagnosed with autism earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: More children are being diagnosed with autism earlier.

sections.label: Work as best form of welfare
sections.summary: Work represents the best form of welfare because it enables dignity and self-respect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Work, I think, in many ways represents the best form of welfare because it enables dignity and self-respect.

sections.label: Redesigning assistance for changing needs
sections.summary: The values and principles guiding assistance do not change, but assistance must be redesigned to meet changing and diverse needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: While the underlying values and principles that guide us do not change, we do need to redesign assistance to meet changing and diverse needs.

sections.label: Mindset shift in supporting Singaporeans
sections.summary: A mindset shift is needed in how Singaporeans are supported and viewed, especially those with disadvantaged circumstances and different abilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Beyond initiatives and programmes, we need a mindset shift in the way we support the needs of fellow Singaporeans, the way we look at them, especially those with more disadvantaged circumstances and different abilities.

sections.label: Third Enabling Master Plan recommendations
sections.summary: The third Enabling Master Plan recommendations set out areas to further strengthen support over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The recommendations in the third Enabling Master Plan set out quite a few areas where we can further strengthen support over the next five years.

sections.label: SSO network rollout and coverage
sections.summary: From 2013, SSOs were rolled out, reaching 24 offices by 2015, with 95% of clients living or working within two kilometres.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In 2013, we started rolling out a network of SSOs to bring more accessible and coordinated social assistance to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: By 2015, we had set up the full network of 24 physical offices across the island.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Today, 95% of SSO clients live or work within two kilometres of an SSO.

sections.label: Officers with social work training
sections.summary: One out of six officers have social work training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: One out of six officers have social work training.

sections.label: Higher income caps for assistance
sections.summary: Since 2014, the monthly household income cap rose from $1,700 to $1,900 and the per-person cap from $550 to $650.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Since 2014, we have increased the monthly household income cap for families seeking Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance from $1,700 to $1,900, and the cap on income per person was raised from $550 to $650.

sections.label: Long-Term Assistance payment increase
sections.summary: Financial support for one-person households on Long-Term Assistance was raised from $450 to $500 a month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The most recent enhancement was last year, where financial support for one-person households on Long-Term Assistance was increased from $450 to $500 a month.

sections.label: Silver Support computed into assistance
sections.summary: For those on Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance also eligible for Silver Support, the Silver Support quantum is computed into overall assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Some of those who receive Silver Support do not need Short-to-Medium Term Assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: But for those who are on Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance but are also eligible for Silver Support, in these cases, we do compute the Silver Support quantum into the overall assistance.

sections.label: SSOs work on debt restructuring
sections.summary: SSOs will work with agencies such as Singapore Power, HDB and Town Councils to see if debt can be restructured.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The SSOs will work with relevant agencies, such as Singapore Power, HDB, Town Councils, to see if the debt can be restructured.

sections.label: ComCare debt repayment and referrals
sections.summary: ComCare cannot repay debts, so families in serious debt are referred to VWOs or organisations like Credit Counselling Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: And these efforts will resolve some of the pressing issues for many of them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: However, ComCare cannot be used for the repayment of debts, to ensure we also do not erode the values of personal responsibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Invariably, you can imagine the kind of behaviours that this can create.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: But we are also aware that, for some families − and I do face them, I think many of us in this House face them − where for whatever reason, the mistakes that they made, wrong decisions in life, they end up mired in quite serious debt and it seems almost impossible to break out of that cycle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: So, in these instances, we would refer them to VWOs who are looking at these issues from a more specialised perspective where they provide debt-related support and advice, or refer them to organisations like the Institute of Financial Literacy and Credit Counselling Singapore.

sections.label: Preventing debt through financial education
sections.summary: Preventing people from getting into debt requires better financial planning advice and education early.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The ideal way is to prevent them from getting into that position in the first place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: That is where providing better financial planning advice and education early would be important.

sections.label: SSO officers plan with recipients
sections.summary: SSO officers work with recipients on an action plan and link them to agencies for other challenges like childcare placement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: There are other difficulties − family problems, relationship problems at home, challenges in finding and holding down stable employment, health concerns, mental health issues and so on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Therefore, our SSO officers need to work with them on an action plan to achieve financial and job stability, link them up with other agencies and community partners that can help them address their other challenges, such as childcare placement.

sections.label: Repeating requests for help
sections.summary: It is painful to keep repeating why help is needed, and SS Net is trying to address this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: But because of that, it is also very painful to keep repeating why you are needing help.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: That is something that we recognise and, through SS Net, we are trying to address some of these issues.

sections.label: Social and employment assistance integration
sections.summary: Two SSOs house social, family and employment services under one roof, and the pilot of one officer delivering both will extend to three more SSOs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Two SSOs − Taman Jurong and Kreta Ayer − have social assistance, family services and employment services all under one roof.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: At the other SSOs, separate appointments for employment assistance are made for clients to see the WSG or e2i officers who come to the SSOs once a week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: This year, we will extend the pilot delivery of both social and employment assistance by the same SSO officer, to three more SSOs.

sections.label: DSP preschool expansion
sections.summary: DSP has helped about 4,000 children across 350 preschools and will expand to another 50 preschools this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Since its inception, it has helped about 4,000 children across 350 preschools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: DSP will be expanded to another 50 preschools this year.

sections.label: Compulsory Education for special needs children
sections.summary: MOE will introduce Compulsory Education for special needs children from 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: MOE will introduce Compulsory Education for special needs children from 2019.

sections.label: Job placements for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: Over three years, SG Enable and VWO partners placed more than 1,200 persons with disabilities into employment through job support and placement assistance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Over the past three years, SG Enable and its VWO partners have collectively placed more than 1,200 persons with disabilities into employment through job support and placement assistance, mainly in the hospitality, food and beverage, retail and administrative support sectors.

sections.label: School-to-Work Transition Programme expansion
sections.summary: The School-to-Work Transition Programme will expand to more SPED schools, from about 30 students last year to about 60 a year by 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: I am heartened to hear the feedback from students, parents and employers about how the programme has allowed students with special needs to acquire work skills, develop good work habits and build a sense of self-worth and confidence to carry out daily activities on their own.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that we will extend the School-to-Work Transition Programme to more SPED schools and students who are work-capable but not work-ready.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The programme will be expanded from supporting about 30 students last year, to about 60 work-capable students a year by 2019.

sections.label: ATF lifetime cap doubled
sections.summary: The 2015 review of the ATF doubled the lifetime cap from $20,000 to $40,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In our recent review of the ATF in 2015, Mr Faisal Manap will be glad to note – and he is aware of it as well – that we doubled the lifetime cap from $20,000 to $40,000.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit to employers
sections.summary: As at December 2016, $59 million in Special Employment Credit went to employers of about 10,000 eligible persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: As at December 2016, $59 million in Special Employment Credit has been given to employers of about 10,000 eligible persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Caregiver support in Third Enabling Masterplan
sections.summary: The Third Enabling Masterplan focuses on more caregiver support, and NCSS with VWOs will develop a caregiver support network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The call for more support for caregivers is a key area of focus in the Third Enabling Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The National Council of Social Service (NCSS), together with VWOs in the sector, will develop a network of support for caregivers.

sections.label: Disability Caregiver Support Centre
sections.summary: As part of the network, NCSS will establish the Disability Caregiver Support Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: As part of this network, NCSS will establish the Disability Caregiver Support Centre.

sections.label: SNTC future care planning services
sections.summary: The SNTC will provide more assistance in future care planning and trust services and step up outreach to caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) will provide more assistance in future care planning and trust services and step up its outreach and engagement efforts to assist caregivers.

sections.label: Adult Disability Hostels and Group Home
sections.summary: Adult Disability Hostels and the Community Group Home serve a small group of higher functioning persons with disabilities without family support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For a small group of higher functioning persons with disabilities where family support is unavailable, we have Adult Disability Hostels and the Community Group Home.

sections.label: Community partner ICT capabilities
sections.summary: The Ministry has introduced initiatives to build community partners' capabilities, and the next Social Service ICT Master Plan phase will automate case management, transition management and case monitoring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Over the years, in terms of building community capabilities, my Ministry has introduced initiatives to build up the capabilities of our community partners so that they can do their work more efficiently and effectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In the next phase of the Social Service ICT Master Plan, we will look into the automation of work processes in terms of case management, transition management, as well as case monitoring.

sections.label: Disability participation and awareness
sections.summary: The Ministry will work with MCCY to give persons with disabilities more sports, cultural, community and youth opportunities, while MSF, NCSS, SG Enable and VWOs promote awareness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For starters, my Ministry will work with MCCY to provide more opportunities for persons with disabilities to participate in sports, cultural, community and youth activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: MSF and our partners, NCSS, SG Enable and VWOs in the disability sector will continue to promote disability awareness and support efforts to bridge the social distance between members of the public and persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Spending on persons with disabilities
sections.summary: Including existing initiatives, around $400 million per year is expected to be spent supporting persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: As shared by the Finance Minister, including existing initiatives, we expect to spend around $400 million per year in supporting persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Childcare and infant care places
sections.summary: Childcare places rose over 40% since 2012 to about 140,000, with 10,000 more planned and infant care places to exceed 8,000 by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since 2012, the number of childcare places has increased by more than 40% to about 140,000 places today.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will continue to support families with small children by adding another 10,000 childcare places in housing estates that have many young families.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will also enhance support for families with infants, by increasing the number of infant care places from 4,000 infants enrolled today, to over 8,000 by 2020.

sections.label: KidSTART programme expansion
sections.summary: Over 300 children in three pilot areas have been assisted, ECDA will partner community organisations for more playgroups, and 1,000 children will be supported over three years.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We hope that KidSTART can continue to create such success stories for parents and their children.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: So far, more than 300 children in Bukit Merah-Kreta Ayer, Boon Lay-Taman Jurong and Geylang Serai have been assisted by this programme.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In the near term, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) will partner community organisations to roll out more community playgroups in areas where the KidSTART programme is being piloted.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We plan to support 1,000 children through KidSTART over the next three years.

sections.label: Parenting programme results and expansion
sections.summary: Parents who completed the programmes reported greater competence, lower stress, improved emotional states and reduced child behavioural problems, and reach will expand to 175 schools by 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Based on our study, parents who completed the programmes reported greater parenting competence, lower parenting stress, improved emotional states and reduced behavioural problems in their children.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We are encouraged by the positive results and plan to expand reach out to 175 schools by 2018.

sections.label: Divorce Support Specialist Agencies
sections.summary: Four Divorce Support Specialist Agencies were appointed to help divorcing couples understand divorce's impact on children and look out for their children's well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Four Divorce Support Specialist Agencies have been appointed to help divorcing couples understand the impact of divorce on their children and look out for their children's well-being.

sections.label: Maintenance Record Officer pilot

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To this end, we are piloting the Maintenance Record Officer initiative, which the Member mentioned, to help the Courts identify recalcitrant defaulters earlier.

sections.label: Adding childcare places

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Over the next year, we will add another 10,000 childcare places and the market should be able to better meet demand within the next few years.

sections.label: Increasing infant care places

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

sections.label: Early childhood diploma intake growth

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Student intake for early childhood diploma courses has also grown by more than 70% last year from 400 to 700 places.

sections.label: Allied Infant Educarers pilot

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To support our expansion plans for infant care, we will need about 1,000 more infant educarers over the next four years.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To meet this large demand, I am pleased to share that my Ministry will pilot a new job role called Allied Infant Educarers.

sentences.text: Educarers will also receive cash awards ranging from $3,000 to $5,000 at the end of each professional development milestone.

sections.label: Advanced Diploma and Study Award

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will extend the SkillsFuture Study Award, worth $5,000, to support preschool teachers embarking on this programme.

sections.label: KidSTART children supported

sentences.text: Since KidSTART was launched in July 2016, we have supported more than 300 children at the pilot sites in Bukit Merah, Kreta Ayer, Boon Lay, Taman Jurong and Geylang Serai.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about the plans for KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Run by MCYC Community Services Society and Boys' Town, these fostering agencies are currently supporting 150 children.

sections.label: Foster families and placements

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

sections.label: Community services partners reach families

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We expect to reach out to 400 families over three years.

sections.label: Youth offending longitudinal study

sections.label: Respondents unsure about family violence

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

sentences.text: Last November, MSF launched a three-year "Break the Silence" campaign to encourage all persons, especially bystanders, who have witnessed family violence to report it early.

sections.label: Vulnerable Adults Act Bill progress

sentences.text: Dr Lily Neo asked about the progress of the Vulnerable Adults Act.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)

sections.label: Family support at all levels

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: At the individual level, we have to make deliberate efforts to make time for our own families and engage them through quality activities and conversations.

sentences.text: Where there is reason to suspect that there is abuse or neglect, everyone has the responsibility to "break the silence" and alert the authorities.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Let us work together to make Singapore a great place to raise children and build strong and resilient families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin

sentences.text: The last major review was in 2015 and the recommended salary increases for social service professionals ranged from 3% to 19%.

sentences.text: In addition to the existing areas of support, we encourage the sector to utilise the VCF to scale up adoption of capability and productivity initiatives.

sentences.text: And in the later part of this year, NCSS will also launch other pre-scoped consultancy projects, in areas with potential productivity improvements, like financial processes and space utilisation.

sections.label: MSF NCSS SkillsFuture framework
sections.summary: Both MSF and NCSS are working with SkillsFuture Singapore to develop this framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Both MSF and NCSS are working with SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) to develop this framework.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Study Award extension
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Study Award will be extended to preschool teachers on the new Advanced Diploma, with 122 individuals having received it to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As Assoc Prof Dr Faishal Ibrahim mentioned, we will extend the SkillsFuture Study Award later this year to support preschool teachers who are embarking on the new Advanced Diploma in Early Childhood Teaching and Learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: To date, a total of 122 individuals in the social service and early childhood sectors have received the SkillsFuture Study Award.

sections.label: NCSS volunteer e-learning module
sections.summary: NCSS is launching an e-learning module for volunteers on working effectively with youths later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: To facilitate the volunteerism efforts, NCSS is launching an e-learning module for volunteers on "Working Effectively with Youths" later this year.

sections.label: NCSS app release target
sections.summary: NCSS targets to release the app at the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: NCSS targets to release the app at the end of the year.

sections.label: Befriending programmes for seniors
sections.summary: Volunteers visit and befriend seniors; three programmes have almost 2,000 volunteers serving over 6,000 seniors, and MOH's Community Befriending Programme is in 33 constituencies with plans for 50 by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As part of these programmes, volunteers pay regular visits to seniors, befriend and engage them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: These three programmes have almost 2,000 volunteers serving over 6,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: MOH's Community Befriending Programme is currently found in 33 constituencies, with plans to expand to 50 constituencies by 2020.

sections.label: Share as One matching donations
sections.summary: Under Share as One, the Government provides dollar-for-dollar matching for new and incremental donations to the SHARE programme till March 2019, with around 300 new companies last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Under Share as One, the Government will provide dollar-for-dollar matching for all new and incremental donations to the SHARE programme till March 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Last year, around 300 new companies came on board, which is an increase of about 11% from 2015.

sections.label: MSF allied infant educarer programme
sections.summary: The speaker is heartened to hear that MSF is going to introduce the allied infant educarer programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: The second question would be, I am heartened to also hear that MSF is going to introduce the allied infant educarer programme.

sections.label: Training Allied Infant Educarers carefully
sections.summary: ECDA works with SEED Institute and anchor operators to train Allied Infant Educarers carefully, with anchor operators nominating only experienced senior infant educarers as mentors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Essentially, we will make sure that the new approach of training will not compromise the quality.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: What will happen is that ECDA works with the SEED Institute and the anchor operators to ensure that we train the Allied Infant Educarers (AIEs) carefully and well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: First, we make sure that the anchor operators nominate only experienced senior infant educarers with the relevant experience as mentors.

sections.label: AIE support for infant services
sections.summary: Additional support by AIEs will translate into better quality services for infants and parents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: With the additional support by the AIEs, this will translate into better quality services for our infants and our parents.

sections.label: Annual youth survey compilation request
sections.summary: A request for the National Youth Council to compile youth-oriented surveys and share them annually with the youth development ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
sentences.text: Could I request that the National Youth Council compile any youth-oriented surveys and share it on an annual basis with the youth development ecosystem so that we can all be on the same page about what we should be looking out for?

sections.label: Reconsidering inclusion as family
sections.summary: A request to reconsider including them sometime down the road as part of family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
sentences.text: Based on that, I would request, could we still reconsider including them sometime down the road as part of family?

sections.label: Numbers for home visitation programmes
sections.summary: The actual number is 389, covering home visitation, KidSTART, and enhanced preschool support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The actual number is more than 300 − which is 389.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For home visitation, it involved 89 infants; for the KidSTART group, it involved 50 children and 45 parents; for the KidSTART enhanced support to preschools, it involved about 250 children across the selected preschools receiving enhanced support.

sections.label: Family nucleus with foreign spouse
sections.summary: A clarification request on whether families with one foreign spouse are considered a family nucleus for HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: So, we need to see how we justify that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: I just want to seek a clarification on whether those families consisting of one foreign spouse, would you still consider them as part of a family nucleus so that they can then purchase and rent HDB flats.

sections.label: Improving volunteer journey with schools
sections.summary: Attention is paid to the volunteer journey, which can be done better, and work with schools is ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: So, you pay attention to the volunteer journey as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I would say that this is something that we can do better and we are working with the schools on this.

sections.label: Shared services and SS Net database
sections.summary: The passage supports developing more shared services and describes SS Net, a database made available to SSOs and eventually Family Service Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: So, the scale is really not quite so ideal in terms of your own resourcing, in terms of your HR system, financial system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are supportive of them trying to develop more shared services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: That is the direction that we would like to see it going so that some of these services can, indeed, be shared and allow the social workers and the set-ups to really focus on the social work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Well, SS Net, which I have mentioned, and some Members will be familiar with, is a database that we have made available not just for SSOs but, eventually, to push down to the Family Service Centres as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: What it means is that the social workers can also tap onto the same base where we look at the individual.

sections.label: Childcare subsidy for mothers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether subsidy levels can be based on full-day or half-day childcare and questions the one-day-a-month attendance requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Parliamentary Secretary rightly pointed out that working mothers usually need full-day childcare and stay-at-home mothers usually need the half-day childcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can we just base the level of subsidy on that, on whether one is full-day or half-day?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: This is so that we do not make it seem like we are penalising stay-at-home mothers, especially at a time when we are urging parents to spend more time with their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: I raised it, that the requirement is just for one day of attendance a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Can we understand why we have set the requirement so low − for only one day of attendance a month?

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment
sections.summary: The speaker asks leave to withdraw their amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
